mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the expected discount rate for future cash flows increases, reducing the present value of equity price expectations and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
failure_condition: In rising-rate regimes, the 5-day forward return is positive or at least not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1 in t-test), or the FEDFUNDS change is not >0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which lowers real discount rates and increases equity valuation multiples, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the forward return is negative or the CPIAUCSL decline is not sustained for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, prompting firms to raise investment in productive capacity and thereby boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or employment growth does not exceed 50,000 in the month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double-digit month-over-month increase during a period of rising consumer demand (implied by HOUST), it suggests accelerating economic activity and a higher growth path for equities, resulting in positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >10% and HOUST is rising in the same month
regime_hint: Demand acceleration with rising industrial activity
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or INDPRO does not show a >10% MoM increase when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the RSAFS index of supply-side imbalances exceeding 5% over three months indicates persistent supply constraints, which can lead central banks to hold rates steady and weigh positively on equity valuations, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >5% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or RSAFS does not decline by >5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 300,000 in a single month triggers a risk-off reaction as investors anticipate slower growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >300,000 in a month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive or the increase in PAYEMS is not >300,000.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2%), the 3-month moving average of consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) falling below 2% suggests deflation, which lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Prolonged monetary easing with sub-2% inflation
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or either FEDFUNDS ≥ 2% or 3-month CPIAUCSL MA ≥ 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) lags the 4-week moving average of GDP (not available in evidence, so use INDPRO trend divergence as proxy) by more than 2 percentage points, it indicates supply chain disorganization that raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 4-week INDPRO MA lags by >2pp relative to implied GDP growth (proxy via trend trajectory)
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive or the lag is ≤2pp in the 4-week MA comparison.
